blocks.en: I received my dear friend's two letters, one for Wednesday and one for Saturday. This is again Wednesday. I do not deserve one for to-day, because I have not answered the former. But, indolent as I am, and averse to writing, the fear of having no more of your pleasing epistles, if I do not contribute to the correspondence, obliges me to take up my pen; and as Mr. B. has kindly sent me word, that he sets out to-morrow to see you, instead of spending this Wednesday evening as I have done its namesakes, in your delightful company, I sit down to spend it in thinking of you, in writing to you, and in reading over and over again your letters.
blocks.zh: 我收到了我亲爱的朋友的两封信，一封是星期三的，一封是星期六的。这又是星期三。我今天不值得回答，因为我还没有回答前者。但是，尽管我很懒惰，也不喜欢写作，但由于担心如果我不写信，就再也得不到你们令人愉快的书信，我不得不拿起笔来； B.先生好心地给我发来消息，说他明天就出发去见你，而不是像我那样在周三晚上与你愉快的陪伴度过，我坐下来用它来想念你，写信给你，一遍又一遍地阅读你的信。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: I am charmed with your description of Paradise, and with your plan of living there; and I approve much of your conclusion, that, in the mean time, we should draw all the good we can from this world. In my opinion, we might all draw more good from it than we do, and suffer less evil, if we would take care not to give too much for whistles. For to me it seems, that most of the unhappy people we meet with, are become so by neglect of that caution.
blocks.zh: 我对你对天堂的描述以及你在那里生活的计划着迷。我非常赞同你的结论，即与此同时，我们应该从这个世界上汲取一切我们能得到的好处。在我看来，如果我们注意不要为口哨付出太多，我们都可以从中获得更多的好处，并减少遭受的邪恶。对我来说，我们遇到的大多数不快乐的人似乎都是因为忽视了这种谨慎而变得如此。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: You ask what I mean? You love stories, and will excuse my telling one of myself.
blocks.zh: 你问我什么意思？你喜欢故事，请原谅我讲一个我自己的故事。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: When I was a child of seven years old, my friends, on a holiday, filled my pocket with coppers. I went directly to a shop where they sold toys for children; and, being charmed with the sound of a whistle, that I met by the way in the hands of another boy, I voluntarily offered and gave all my money for one. I then came home, and went whistling all over the house, much pleased with my whistle, but disturbing all the family. My brothers, and sisters, and cousins, understanding the bargain I had made, told me I had given four times as much for it as it was worth; put me in mind what good things I might have bought with the rest of the money; and laughed at me so much for my folly, that I cried with vexation; and the reflection gave me more chagrin than the whistle gave me pleasure.
blocks.zh: 当我七岁的时候，我的朋友们在假期里给我的口袋装满了铜板。我直接去了一家卖儿童玩具的商店；我被另一个男孩手中的哨声迷住了，我自愿献出我所有的钱买一个。然后我回到家，在整个房子里吹口哨，对我的口哨很满意，但打扰了全家人。我的兄弟姐妹和表兄弟姐妹了解了我所做的交易，并告诉我，我为此付出了四倍的代价；我的钱是它的价值的四倍。让我记住我可以用剩下的钱买什么好东西；他们嘲笑我的愚蠢，使我懊恼地哭泣。倒影给我带来的懊恼比口哨给我带来的快乐还要多。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: This however was afterwards of use to me, the impression continuing on my mind; so that often, when I was tempted to buy some unnecessary thing, I said to myself, Don't give too much for the whistle; and I saved my money.
blocks.zh: 然而，这后来对我有用，这个印象一直留在我的脑海里。因此，当我经常想买一些不必要的东西时，我对自己说，不要为哨子付出太多；我省了钱。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As I grew up, came into the world, and observed the actions of men, I thought I met with many, very many, who gave too much for the whistle.
blocks.zh: 当我长大，来到这个世界，观察人们的行为时，我想我遇到了很多很多人，他们为哨子付出了太多。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: When I saw one too ambitious of court favour, sacrificing his time in attendance on levees, his repose, his liberty, his virtue, and perhaps his friends, to attain it, I have said to myself, This man gives too much for his whistle.
blocks.zh: 当我看到一个野心勃勃的宫廷恩惠者，牺牲了他在堤坝上的时间、他的休息、他的自由、他的美德，也许还有他的朋友来获得它时，我对自己说，这个人为了他的哨子付出了太多。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: When I saw another fond of popularity, constantly employing himself in political bustles, neglecting his own affairs, and ruining them by that neglect, He pays, indeed, said I, too much for his whistle.
blocks.zh: 当我看到另一个喜欢受欢迎的人，不断地忙于政治喧嚣，忽视自己的事情，并因此而毁掉自己的事情时，我说，他确实为他的哨子付出了太多的代价。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: If I knew a miser, who gave up every kind of comfortable living, all the pleasure of doing good to others, all the esteem of his fellow-citizens, and the joys of benevolent friendship, for the sake of accumulating wealth, Poor man, said I, you pay too much for your whistle.
blocks.zh: 如果我认识一个守财奴，他为了积累财富而放弃了一切舒适的生活、所有为他人行善的乐趣、所有同胞的尊重以及仁慈友谊的乐趣，可怜的人，我说，你为你的哨子付出了太多的代价。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: When I met with a man of pleasure, sacrificing every laudable improvement of the mind, or of his fortune, to mere corporeal sensations, and ruining his health in their pursuit, Mistaken man, said I, you are providing pain for yourself, instead of pleasure; you give too much for your whistle.
blocks.zh: 当我遇到一个享乐的人时，他为了纯粹的肉体感觉而牺牲了精神或财富上每一个值得称赞的进步，并在追求快乐的过程中毁掉了他的健康，我说，这个错误的人，你给自己带来了痛苦，而不是快乐；你为你的哨子付出了太多。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: If I see one fond of appearance, or fine clothes, fine houses, fine furniture, fine equipages, all above his fortune, for which he contracts debts, and ends his career in a prison, Alas! say I, he has paid dear, very dear, for his whistle.
blocks.zh: 若我见一个人喜爱外表，或漂亮的衣服、漂亮的房子、漂亮的家具、漂亮的装备，都超过了他的财富，而他为此负债累累，而在监狱中结束了他的职业生涯，唉！我说，他为他的哨子付出了昂贵的、非常昂贵的代价。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: When I see a beautiful, sweet-tempered girl married to an ill-natured brute of a husband, What a pity, say I, that she should pay so much for a whistle!
blocks.zh: 当我看到一个美丽、性情温和的女孩嫁给了一个脾气暴躁的丈夫时，我说，她为一只哨子付出这么多代价，真是太遗憾了！
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: In short, I conceive that great part of the miseries of mankind are brought upon them by the false estimates they have made of the value of things, and by their giving too much for their whistles.
blocks.zh: 简而言之，我认为人类的大部分苦难都是由于他们对事物价值的错误估计以及他们为口哨付出太多而造成的。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Yet I ought to have charity for these unhappy people, when I consider, that, with all this wisdom of which I am boasting, there are certain things in the world so tempting, for example, the apples of King John, which happily are not to be bought; for if they were put to sale by auction, I might very easily be led to ruin myself in the purchase, and find that I had once more given too much for the whistle.
blocks.zh: 然而，当我考虑到，以我所吹嘘的所有智慧，世界上有些东西如此诱人时，我应该对这些不幸的人抱有仁慈，例如，约翰国王的苹果，幸运的是，它们是买不到的；因为如果它们被拍卖，我可能很容易在购买中毁掉自己，并发现我再次为哨子付出了太多。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Adieu, my dear friend, and believe me ever yours very sincerely and with unalterable affection,
blocks.zh: 再见，我亲爱的朋友，请相信我永远是你的真诚和不可改变的感情，
